comparison.text: Reminder: Delhi residents are losing 8.2 years of life expectancy to PM2.5, per the AQLI 2025 report. The average Indian loses 3.5.
comparison.caveat: Relative to permanent attainment of the WHO 5 ug/m3 guideline. A statistical average across the population, not a personal prediction.

comparison.text: Kids breathe faster than adults, so they absorb more of this per kilo. They also live closer to the ground, where some pollutants peak. WHO's words, not ours.
comparison.source_name: WHO, More than 90% of the world's children breathe toxic air every day (2018)
comparison.caveat: Direct WHO statements: children 'breathe more rapidly than adults and so absorb more pollutants' and 'live closer to the ground, where some pollutants reach peak concentrations'.

comparison.text: If every day were like today, you would live at 6x the WHO annual safe level.
comparison.source_name: WHO, 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines (PM2.5 annual average 5 ug/m3)
comparison.caveat: Compares one day against an annual guideline, so it describes a hypothetical year of days like today, not your actual annual exposure.

comparison.text: Today's air is worse than 98 percent of days this season in Bengaluru. Ranked, logged, versioned.
comparison.caveat: Season means the trailing 90 days of this project's own observations. Small archive early on means noisy percentiles, and the repo shows exactly how small.

comparison.text: Nashik today is 4x the air of Pune, the cleanest city we track. Same country, different lungs.
comparison.caveat: Same-day comparison across the five tracked cities using the same measurement rule for each. Only shown when the ratio is at least 1.5.
